primary_source.title: AutoResearchBench: Benchmarking AI Agents on Complex Scientific Literature Discovery
verified_claims: The benchmark separates Deep Research (progressive multi-step target-paper discovery) from Wide Research (collecting all papers satisfying open-ended conditions).
The strongest reported systems reach only 9.39% accuracy on Deep Research and 9.31% IoU on Wide Research; many strong baselines are below 5%.
The authors publicly release the dataset, evaluation pipeline, and code.
scope_limits: This is strong quantitative bottleneck evidence for autonomous scientific-literature discovery, not evidence that a particular dedicated search subsystem solves the bottleneck.
No matched intervention ablation was verified that compares a dedicated iterative literature subsystem against an otherwise identical research agent.
No independent replication/failure study of the benchmark or candidate mechanism was verified in this pass.

assessment.reason: Primary quantitative benchmark and released code/data strongly establish the literature-discovery bottleneck, but they do not causally validate the candidate subsystem. Reproducibility-artifact support improves; intervention evidence does not.
assessment.needed_to_promote: A matched or randomized intervention showing that an explicit literature-discovery/search subsystem materially improves downstream research quality or discovery under a controlled budget, ideally with independent replication or failure analysis.
